items.title: Mohammed ben Salmane à Paris : Macron déroule le tapis rouge
items.description: Mohammed ben Salmane est a Paris les 23 et 24 août pour une visite officielle destinee a approfondir le rapprochement entre la France et l'Arabie saoudite. Le 23 août, Emmanuel Macron et le prince heritier ont assiste ensemble a la cloture de la Coupe du monde d'e-sport, organisee pour la premiere fois hors du royaume. Ce lundi 24 août, place a la politique et aux affaires : entretien a l'elysee, premier Conseil de partenariat strategique franco-saoudien et ceremonie de signatures. Paris annonce de « nombreux accords », notamment dans les transports, l'energie et la sante. Une table ronde reunit egalement dirigeants et entreprises autour de l'industrie, de la logistique, de l'intelligence artificielle et des infrastructures numeriques. Macron entend surtout attirer davantage d'investissements saoudiens en France. Pour oublier le tumulte en interne Mais la visite illustre aussi le spectaculaire changement de regard de l'elysee sur MBS. En 2022, sa premiere venue a Paris apres l'assassinat du journaliste Jamal Khashoggi avait provoque une vive polemique. Quatre ans plus tard, les reserves semblent largement releguees au second plan : Macron presente desormais le dirigeant saoudien comme un partenaire essentiel pour la stabilite regionale, les investissements et la securite energetique. Le president francais mise ainsi sur une relation avec un royaume devenu incontournable, quitte a faire passer les critiques sur les droits humains derriere les imperatifs economiques et diplomatiques. Les deux dirigeants doivent notamment evoquer Gaza, le Liban, la Syrie et la crise autour du detroit d'Ormuz, ainsi que la diversification des routes d'approvisionnement energetique. Pour Macron, fragilise sur la scene interieure, la reception de MBS permet aussi d'afficher une France encore capable de dialoguer avec l'une des puissances centrales du Moyen-Orient.

items.title: Burkina Faso-Chine: les deux pays affinent les axes de coopération médiatique
items.description: BURKINA-FASO-CHINE-COOPERATION-MEDIATIQUE Burkina Faso-Chine: les deux pays affinent les axes de coopération médiatique Ouagadougou, 24 août 2026 (AIB) – Le Burkina Faso et la Chine entendent renforcer leur coopération médiatique à travers le partage de contenus, le transfert de technologies et la formation des professionnels de l’information et de la communication. C’est ce qui ressort d’un entretien entre le ministre de la Communication, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo et le vice-ministre chinois de l’Administration nationale de la Radio et de la Télévision, Liu Jianguo, en marge du 7e Forum sur la Coopération des médias Sino-Africains, tenu du 19 au 21 août 2026 à Pékin. Dans le cadre du partage de contenus, les deux parties ont convenu d’examiner les possibilités de diffusion de programmes documentaires ainsi que de productions cinématographiques et audiovisuelles majeures entre la Radiodiffusion-Télévision du Burkina (RTB) et l’une des télévisions publiques chinoises. Cette initiative vise à favoriser la découverte réciproque des cultures des deux peuples. Une convention viendra formaliser ce premier volet du partenariat. Le Burkina Faso entend également bénéficier de l’expérience technologique chinoise pour mettre à niveau ses équipements audiovisuels et moderniser ses infrastructures médiatiques. Les deux parties ont, par ailleurs, réaffirmé leur volonté de poursuivre les sessions de formation et les échanges d’expériences entre les professionnels de l’information et de la communication, des secteurs public et privé. Au terme de l’audience, le ministre Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo s’est réjoui de la posture chinoise, qui s’inscrit, selon lui, dans un partenariat stratégique permettant aux deux peuples de mieux se découvrir à travers la coopération culturelle et médiatique. Agence d'information du Burkina DCRP-MCCAT

items.title: 2027: Village Boys Movement mobilises Abia grassroots for Obi
items.description: By Steve Oko The Village Boys Movement, a support group for the presidential aspiration of Mr Peter Obi, has commenced grassroots mobilisation in Abia State ahead of the 2027 general elections, vowing to ensure that the people’s votes are protected and counted. The Abia State chapter of the movement made this known in Umuahia while explaining its mission and objectives during a rally, describing itself as a national grassroots platform for Nigerians who believe in Obi’s vision for the country. The state leader, Barrister Nkasiobi Madumere, who is addressed as the “Headmistress,” said the movement’s immediate objective was to take Obi’s message to the grassroots, mobilise voters and sensitise them on the need to defend their votes in 2027. She said the group was committed to delivering Nigeria to Obi and ensuring that no form of electoral malpractice would frustrate the people’s mandate. According to her, the movement comprises Nigerians across political divides who believe that Obi has the capacity and willingness to address the country’s challenges. “We are grassroots mobilisers. We want good governance, a better Nigeria and a Nigeria that works for all of us,” she said. She explained that the movement’s strategy was to return to the villages where most Nigerians came from, mobilise and sensitise the people and prepare them to protect their votes. The Abia leader, however, clarified that the Village Boys Movement was not an NDC structure, despite Obi’s presidential candidacy being under the party. She said the movement was a national platform headed by its National Headmaster, Mazi Tochukwu Ezoke, with other national officers including Ben Chukwu and Dr Justin Kingland. She stressed that membership was open to Obi supporters irrespective of their political party, including members of the Labour Party, PDP and other parties. “This is a structure for people who believe in Obi’s candidacy. Anybody who supports Obi and wants him to become president is welcome on this platform,” she said. She added that the movement would also work with willing candidates contesting under the NDC while maintaining its identity as an independent support platform for Obi. The group said its mobilisation drive would culminate in a stronger grassroots network across Abia and other states, with emphasis on voter sensitisation, electoral participation and protection of the ballot. items.title: Gamou de Tivaouane: La grande vague de la foi avant le jour J
items.description: À quarante-huit heures du Mawlid 2026, Tivaouane est en pleine effervescence. Dès le vendredi 21 août, coïncidant avec la Hadratoul Jummah, des milliers de fidèles venus de toutes les régions du Sénégal et de la sous-région ont déferlé sur la capitale de la Tijaniyya. La ville est partagée entre ferveur spirituelle lors des ziarras, embouteillages monstres dans les ruelles barrées et commerçants dans l’attente des acheteurs. TIVAOUANE – Le Mawlid est prévu ce mardi. Mais déjà, les pèlerins déferlent sur la capitale de la Tijaniyya, en provenance de diverses localités du pays et même de la sous-région. Si certains sont présents depuis le début du Burd, la grande masse a pris d’assaut la cité religieuse dès le vendredi pour assister à la prière hebdomadaire, accomplir la Hadrat et effectuer leurs ziarras avant le jour J. Écharpe blanche aux effigies de Seydi El Hadj Malick et de Cheikh Tidiane Chérif autour du cou, El Hadji Malick Diop a quitté Kaffrine ce même jour pour assister à la prière du vendredi. Croisé à l’entrée de la mosquée Serigne Babacar Sy, il ne peut contenir son émotion après sa ziarra : « J’ai le cœur rempli de joie à chaque fois que je viens ici. En plus du ziar, j’en profite pour solliciter des prières », confie-t-il en égrenant son chapelet. Awa Ndiaye, dite « Talibé Cheikh », partage cette même ferveur. Assise sur l’esplanade de la mosquée Serigne Babacar, la septuagénaire réajuste un grand tableau du marabout que trois jeunes femmes viennent de lui remettre. Elle caresse le cadre et lance : « Je ne vis que pour lui ». La vieille dame a quitté Pout depuis mercredi. « J’ai l’habitude d’assister au Gamou depuis toute petite ; je venais avec mon père. J’ai même assisté à la fondation de la mosquée », raconte-t-elle en désignant du doigt l’endroit où se trouvait autrefois un puits. Avec l’âge, elle préfère désormais arriver tôt pour éviter les bousculades qui l’empêchent de communier sereinement avec son guide. En effet, plus le jour J approche, plus la foule se densifie. Ce dimanche, les files ininterrompues de véhicules rendent les routes et les trottoirs trop étroits pour les piétons, contraints de se frayer un chemin entre automobiles, charrettes et conducteurs de motos « Jakarta ». En raison des barrières érigées par la police, l’accès à certains secteurs est devenu très difficile. Les abords des différents mausolées sont envahis par des marées humaines où surviennent parfois de légères bousculades, exaspérant par moments certains membres du Coskas. « Plus on se rapproche du Gamou, plus le travail d’organisation devient compliqué », explique Matar Sarr, de la commission d’ordre. Le jeune homme, posté à la Zawiya Seydi El Hadj Malick, relativise aussitôt. «Nous sommes les soldats de la Khadra, nous nous efforçons donc de supporter certains écarts de comportement. Au fond, les fidèles sont simplement submergés par l’impatience de faire leur ziarra », déclare-t-il, sourire en coin. Traînant une grande valise rose surmontée d’une valisette assortie, téléphone à l’oreille, Awa Gaye tente de se localiser près du domicile de Serigne Habib Sy Mansour. « J’ai tellement marché… Le véhicule ne pouvait plus avancer », se plaint-elle en essuyant la sueur qui perle sur son visage. Après plusieurs minutes de marche, la jeune Aminata dépose son lourd sac à l’ombre d’un arbre, près d’un vendeur de cocos. Après une grande inspiration, elle réalise qu’il lui reste encore du chemin. « Si ma tenue avait été prête, je serais venue vendredi avec mes cousines pour m’éviter cette peine », regrette-t-elle. Moussa Dieng déplore lui aussi que leur car « Ndiaga Ndiaye », loué depuis Louga, n’ait pu atteindre leur site d’accueil. Avec ses proches, il décharge ventilateurs, ustensiles de cuisine et matelas sur lesquels sautillent déjà les enfants. « Je les plains. Ils auraient dû venir plus tôt », lance Abdoulaye Diop. Ce jeune vendeur d’habits venu de Touba s’inquiète surtout pour sa marchandise. « Je peine à vendre. Les pèlerins cherchent d’abord à rejoindre leur logement, car ils arrivent épuisés et chargés », soutient-il. Son collègue Modou Ndiaye, fort de ses cinq ans d’expérience, se veut rassurant. « Chaque année, c’est calme au début. Mais le jour J et le lendemain du Gamou, les clients achètent massivement des cadeaux », déclare-t-il. Pour Marième Kane, vendeuse de « meulfeuh », un tissu venu de Mauritanie, le constat est plus amer. Selon elle, même s’il y a de la foule les derniers jours, les bénéfices ne sont plus ce qu’ils étaient. « Cela fait sept ans que je viens à Tivaouane et Ndiassane, et je remarque qu’il est de plus en plus difficile d’écouler la marchandise », confie-t-elle au cœur d’un marché saturé de sonorités mêlant musiques, khassaïdes, chants tidianes et cris de marchands. Par Fatou SY (Texte) – Mbacké BÂ (Photos)

items.title: What It Takes to Reclaim Your Attention Span
items.description: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube | Pocket Casts Of all the potential effects of using smartphones, the one that seems to inspire the most anxiety is what scrolling could be doing to people’s attention. On social media (ironically), many people express a desire to “heal” their attention spans from the damage they feel technology has done. They’re picking up on something real. In one 2025 study , researchers found that blocking the internet on people’s phones for two weeks led to improvements in sustained attention equivalent to reversing 10 years of cognitive decline. In this final episode of How to Touch Grass , host Julie Beck embarks on an experiment to see if she can heal her own attention span. Beck and co-host Natalie Brennan also hear from Jenny Odell, the author of How to Do Nothing and Saving Time , about how Odell’s antagonism for her phone actually helped her make peace with it, and how nature can teach us to pay deeper attention to the world around us. The following is a transcript of the episode: [ Music ] Julie Beck: Are you happy with your relationship with your phone, or are you not happy with it? Person 1: I wish I could reduce some of the Instagram Reel-ing, particularly at night, where I kind of go down the rabbit hole and it’s like, Oh my God, it’s midnight. Beck: Oh, yeah. I’ve been there. It’s like lost time. You know like when the aliens come and they get you, and then they put you back down, and it’s just lost time. Person 2: It has impacted my attention span. I get bored after half a paragraph of reading. Beck: Do you have a sense in your mind of when you noticed that you feel like your attention span was getting worse? Person 2: Probably been, like, since the start of COVID, probably in the last five years. Person 3: The thing that kills me sometimes is how much I want to look stuff up in conversations. I still constantly have a few books that I’m trying to read through and trying to rebuild attention, or something like that. Beck: I’m Julie Beck, a staff writer at The Atlantic . Natalie Brennan: And I’m Natalie Brennan, a producer at The Atlantic . Beck: This is How to Touch Grass . [ Birds chirping ] Brennan: Julie, attention is one of the biggest things we’ve heard people talk about when they are renegotiating their relationship to their phone. Beck: Ironically, I feel like every time I go on social media these days, I see someone talking about how they’re trying to heal their attention span from technology that they’re currently using. Brennan: ( Laughs .) Yes. Beck: And it’s always that word too, heal . It’s like we’re sick or we’re injured, and we must heal. Brennan: Is it something that you’ve been worried about? Beck: I do worry about my attention sometimes. Like every time I go to the gym lately, I forget to lock the locker that they have in the locker room. I put my stuff in there; I shut the door. Brennan: And you don’t lock? Beck: Then I guess I simply walk away. Brennan: Huh! Beck : And I don’t realize until I get back that—I mean, no one has taken my stuff, luckily, so it’s all good. Good Samaritans out there. But that has happened not once, not twice, more than twice. ( Laughs. ) Brennan: I guess the way that the attention-span thing comes up for me the most is when I think about the number of hours that I spend on my phone. Beck: You’re pouring your attention into that phone. Brennan: Yeah, I see those as very interconnected. But I’ve also noticed that I very actively try not to think about it. I rush to swipe away the screen-time notification every Sunday. Obviously, that anxiety points to the fact that I want to have a different relationship with my phone, right? Beck: What do you think has stopped you from actively trying to get that screen time down? Brennan: I think it’s scary to sit with ourselves when we have grown really accustomed to all the stimuli. Beck: Mmm. Love stimuli. [ Music ] Jenny Odell: We talk a lot about, you know, looking at your phone as a negative thing, and we talk about it in the negative, right? Like, I wanna do less of this thing. There’s this thing that I do a lot; I wanna do less of it . And there’s not as much talk about what I wanna do more of . Beck: That’s Jenny Odell, the author of How to Do Nothing . When that book came out in 2019, and I remember at the time it was one of the first things I read that really raised a concern about what modern technology and social media were doing specifically to people’s attention. So now it’s seven years later, and I asked Jenny how her thinking has evolved and how she’s doing with her own screen-time habits. Odell: I mean, I’m … [( Laughs. )] Look, I’m doing great. Beck: That’s—I’m so happy to hear it. I can’t say the same. ( Laughs. ) Odell: I’m okay with my relationship with my phone and screen time. Beck: So can you walk me through a little bit? Odell: Yeah. I would say, like, part of the attention economy is the selling of quick fixes when, you know, habits form over time. They’re like grooves, right? Like, they need to be sort of formed over time. And so … Beck: Like, geologically. Odell: Yes, exactly. And I think, you know, if you try to, say, go cold turkey, it can be frustrating when you don’t see immediate results. Beck: Yeah. Odell: Or even within a couple of months, right? And then in that meantime, there’s all this uphill struggle of, like, your friends are still doing it. You need to be on Instagram to see this and that, and there’s just muscle-memory things, things you’re used to. You get up in the morning; you look at your phone. These are just—that’s hard. Like, those things are really ingrained, especially, I think, if you’re younger. I’m good now. But I just wanna stress that it took some time, and in that time there’s a little bit of a leap of faith. Beck: Yeah. I mean, I deleted TikTok off my phone for the third or fourth time, who’s counting? But like you were saying, the muscle memory of, like, the thumb going up and down, has just transferred to Instagram unfortunately. So we gotta work on that. Odell: I would say there’s, honestly, you know, I’m almost 40. Actually standing, like, with your very heavy head, like on your neck; when you get older, you start to notice the problems from that, and it’s like that is another kind of physical limit. I can’t sit at a computer for that long without injuring myself. And then I think I really had to think about my relationship to the news was a really big one that I hadn’t quite figured out. When you’re kind of scrolling, you're scrolling through it, you’re not really deeply engaging with any one particular issue. Beck: Yeah. Odell: You’re just seeing a list of bad things, and they’re bad in all different kinds of ways, and they’re terrible. Like, even just sitting with one of those things produces this paralysis. It’s like, in order to do something, you need an orientation toward the future and a situation in which you feel that you have some agency. There are certain things that I have started to do in the last couple years. One of them is volunteering at a native-plant-restoration project every week. I’ve also been going to a lot of repair fairs. Also kind of volunteering-type things that are in person. Beck: Where you bring like a broken toaster or something— Odell: Yeah.. Beck: —and learn how to fix it. Odell : And learn how to fix it. Yeah. Totally. When I’m there, there is no desire to look at my phone. Like, it’s just so far from my mind, and it has this weird lasting effect throughout the week, actually, because I had this experience that was so direct, that was so meaningful. Beck: And tell me what is the good thing about the repair café, about the, you know, weeding the native plants? Like, what is the good thing? Odell: I think, you know, some of it is just recognition. I think we as humans, we want to be socially recognized, right? We want to feel seen. We wanna feel heard. We wanna feel welcomed. You know, it’s like Cheers or whatever. Beck: ( Laughs. ) Odell: Like, you wanna walk into a room and have people be like, Hey, it’s you. I know you.I’m happy to see you . This is just kind of like a really basic thing that we want. I kinda think that social media, especially early on, the evil genius of it was that it was hijacking that. And so I feel like these are in-person events. I feel incredibly recognized and acknowledged. And then it’s like, when you feel This is the real thing , it becomes very obvious what is not the real thing. That’s a big part of it. And I think you’re there. You have a shared project. You’re getting some traction with something, right? Instead of just sort of constantly being washed over with information and not really having anything to grasp onto. Beck: For most people in this day and age, totally going without a smartphone just isn’t possible, or at least not practical. Like, the infrastructure of society, you know, they’ve got the QR-code menu at the restaurant, the stores are all accepting Apple Pay and Google Pay, and so many websites require you to receive a text and then put the code in to even get in there. So trying to resist getting sucked into your phone just feels like resisting the inevitable sometimes. Have you found a way to resolve this tension for yourself? Odell: I live in the same society you’re describing, and I just used my phone to pay for lunch before this. But then I put it away. Beck: Mmm. Odell: I use the phrase standing apart as a way of kind of not leaving or believing in the fantasy of escape from something, and just sort of being like, I’m standing in a position from which I can see the thing. Beck: You’re not running away from it or— Odell: But I have critical distance. And I think about something like food. You know, you go to the grocery store and, I mean, depending on the grocery store you’re in, you kind of understand that 80 percent of the food in it is bad for you. We kinda know that, right? It has been that way long enough. Beck: Doesn’t stop me from getting the Flamin’ Hot Cheetos, but yes. I do know. Odell: ( Laughs. ) But it’s just this understanding that that space is just not set up for me to thrive. Beck: Mm. Odell: And I think that it’s helpful to maybe transpose that to your phone. What is a phone? A phone is a communication device. What I want from this is communication. The apps, you know, social media in particular, are not designed for you to thrive. They are designed for the opposite. ( Laughs. ) These are actively bad for me, and I won’t feel good. For me, it’s sort of a level of acceptance of, like, antagonism has been helpful. Where it’s like, I’m never going to have a peaceful relationship with that universe, and I’m just gonna kind of accept that and take what I need and leave. Beck: You know, recently I hear so many people, both online and in real life, talking about, “healing their attention spans” from the damage that they feel like technology has done. And I’m curious why, of all the things, you think people are worried about their attention specifically. Odell: One would hope that what you pay attention to is what is important to you. That’s an ideal situation. Beck: Not always the case. Odell: Right, exactly. So if you’re not paying attention to things that are important to you, there’s something, I think, like, deeply unsettling about that on the level of identity because it’s like, Am I even who I am? Right? Am I who I want to be if I’m paying my attention to something that I don’t feel I ever chose? Beck: Yeah. Odell: I think it really deeply affects people on the level of, like, self-control and their sort of understanding of their identity. Beck: Yeah. Well, it seems like the solution that many people have landed on for healing their attention span is just trying to be online less, however they can. So do you think that logging off is the answer, or no? Odell: I think that the best approach, personally, is to just treat it as an experiment. Honestly, it makes it interesting, like I’m a curious person and I’m curious about myself and my own reaction to things. Kind of being like, Okay, I’m gonna try this. I’m gonna see what happens when I try this. [ Music ] Beck: Natalie, immediately after this interview, I really felt the itch to do what Jenny said—to try an experiment. And when I was thinking about how to do that, I remembered this study I had seen from 2025 where researchers blocked the internet on people’s smartphones for two weeks. Brennan: Okay. Beck: And just doing that, they found that the improvement to people’' sustained attention was equivalent to reversing 10 years of cognitive decline. Brennan: After two weeks? Beck: After two weeks. Brennan: That discrepancy feels huge. Beck: It’s huge. So I tried the experiment on myself for two weeks. Now, I didn’t perfectly replicate the conditions of the 2025 study, to be clear. They blocked mobile internet using an app called Freedom. I used, instead, this device called a Brick. Brennan: Huge among my friends. Beck: Oh, your friends are all into it. Brennan: Yes. Beck: Okay, so you know. So I used this device. I picked all the apps I was gonna block, and you have to physically touch your phone to the device to unlock it. Brennan: Right. Beck: I tried to, you know, keep all of the things that would allow me to communicate with other people, and so I blocked all games; I blocked all social media, email, Slack, internet browsers, and most internet-connected apps. Brennan: Okay. Beck: So I blocked all of that for 23 hours a day. I was allowed one hour of non-Bricked time if I needed or wanted it. And I could do whatever I wanted on a computer, same as in the study. It was only the phone that was restricted. Brennan: And how were you going to test this? Beck: So I got in touch with someone from that 2025 study, and they shared an attention pre-test with me and a self-report questionnaire. So I took those for a baseline. Brennan: How long was the test? Beck: It felt like 1,000 hours. Brennan: Totally. ( Laughs. ) Beck: I think he told me it’s actually, like, eight minutes. ( Laughs. ) I did both of those things before I started the experiment, and then I took them again at the end of the experiment. And I agreed to record a little audio diary along the way. [ Music ] Beck: Captain’s log, day one. My phone has been Bricked pretty much all day. I’ve definitely been kinda low energy. I don’t know if that’s, like, dopamine withdrawal. I’ve definitely been carrying my phone around with me everywhere even though there’s not really that much for me to look at. Morning, it’s day two. My husband is out of town right now, so it is daunting to have two of my biggest sources of entertainment, my husband and my phone, unavailable to me at this time, but we persevere. It is Saturday. It’s my first full weekend day. I ordered a big order of yarn, so I have a lot of knitting and crochet stuff to work on. Good morning, it’s day five. Knitting right now. Joe and I went birding. The one thing that I am noticing mood-wise is that I do feel pretty calm, like maybe more calm than usual. Brennan: OK, Julie! First check-in. What off the bat did you think you were going to do more of with your time that you didn’t wind up doing? Beck: Using the phone as a phone, as a communication device. Actually, like, calling my loved ones to catch up, you know, what the phone was invented for. Shout-out Alexander Graham Bell. But I think because I had blocked so much, and I was getting more used to just not having my phone on me and in my hand at all times, I was just thinking about my phone less overall, which was the goal.But I kinda come to think that as much as the distraction of the phone, like, has a cost, there’s also a cost to putting more distance there, because the phone is where the people are. Brennan: It’s interesting how much our relationship to our phones is intertwined with our relationship to others. Beck: Yeah. Brennan: When we overuse our phones, that isn’t good for our relationships, and the way we use our phones is definitely influenced by other people. [ Music ] Odell: I think we don’t realize how much of our habits kind of live in other people. Like, think about it. When do you pick up your phone? It’s when the person you’re talking to picks up their phone, right? Like, the person picks up their phone; what are you gonna do? Sit there? Stare into space? That habit, like, lives between people. Beck: It’s so true, because my friends will, you know, text me TikToks still even though I am trying to get off TikTok. And then if I’m like, Okay, I’ll just watch the, like, Lord of the Rings meme that they sent me , of course my phone prompts me like, Don’t you wanna download TikTok again? And so it is, like, sort of driven by, like, the relationship of wanting to see this meme. But I guess my bigger question is: Is logging off to pay attention to something else in the real world actually better, or is it just different? Odell: I always think about, like, if you saw someone hiking and looking at their phone, you could be like, That’s so depressing. But then it’s like, what if they’re looking at iNaturalist? Beck: Yeah. Odell: And they’re, like, identifying a plant. There are good things on the phone; there are bad things on the phone. There are good things IRL; there are bad things IRL. One thing that you can say is that the sort of quality of attention that one often experiences on the phone with things like social media is pretty narrow versus things off the phone. There are so many different kinds of experience, so many different scales of time, so many different scales of space. I love seeing movies in a movie theater. Beck: Oh, yeah. Me too. Odell: I’m like a movie-theater junkie. I love to see horror movies in a theater. Beck: Oh. Not me. Odell: So there’s things like that, but then there’s things like looking at a very small bird in your neighborhood, or being at a table with a group of people and being part of a conversation. Like, these are all just so different. Even if you think about your body in those spaces; it’s so different. I think it’s good to have a variety of different contexts for your attention.I think that’s probably healthy. [ Music ] Beck: We’re gonna take a quick break but when we come back: how the way we think about our phones affects the ways we use them. Odell: I think about it more as like: When I look at it as an object, it looks like a tool. And it did not look like a tool to me before. It looked like a black hole. Beck: Like a portal to the underworld or something. Brennan: Plus, did Julie fix her attention span? The results of her experiment, coming up. [ Break ] Beck: So day six, and wouldn’t you freaking know it, I did the exact same thing at the gym again. Sure enough, I forgot to lock it again . I’m legitimately concerned. Anyway, my attention is not fixed yet! Good morning. It’s day seven of the experiment. My average screen time is down 74 percent from last week. I certainly haven’t been, like a perfect screen-abstinent person this week. I’ve watched plenty of TV. I have been able to, I think, focus a bit better. I read 200 pages of my book yesterday. I wonder how much of this could be achieved without such a draconian approach. I’ve been pretty surprised by how quickly I kind of, like, submitted. But yeah, just how quickly the cravings to check my phone all the time really receded. Brennan: Julie, day 7 was midway through your experiment. What started to shift for you by that point? Did the way you think about your phone start to change? Beck: I think what you learn, or at least what I learned when you block access to almost everything on your phone, is that the phone is not just one thing. There’s a lot of different stuff in there. Like— Brennan: Yeah. Beck: —you know? I think in our frustration with our attention span sometimes, people, myself included, will demonize the phone as a device. Like, smartphones are evil. Smartphones are sucking our life force, and they’re making us stupid, and that kind of flattens the problem, I think. What kept coming up for me is there’s a lot of different things I turn to my phone for, and some of them are more problematic than others. Like, checking the weather is, uh, very helpful. Brennan: You made a mistake in blocking that one ( Laughs. ) Beck: I did. Like, I realized that actually the first day. But I suppose that is the point of the experiment, right? To figure out which parts of my phone are actually adding to my life and which are taking away from it. [ Music ] Beck: Jenny, have you heard of these devices that block certain apps on your phone? There’s the Freedom app, the Unplug, the Brick device. Odell: Yeah. Beck : What do you think of the recent popularity of these things? Odell: Honestly, I’m all for it. I don’t use any—I’m not trying to brag. I don’t need them. I think they’re great. There’s one in particular that I think is called SocialFocus, and it lets you kind of change the appearance of websites. Like, you could go to YouTube and not see the auto suggestions, for example. Beck: Mmm. Odell: Or maybe not see comments. It kind of allows you to change what you see. And I think there was a Chrome extension that came out called News Feed Eradicator. And guess what happened? I stopped going to Facebook. And I didn’t decide to do that. It was because the News Feed is there to keep you on Facebook. So if you eradicate it, replace it with some sort of mindfulness quote, you go to the site; it’s inert. It can’t grab you in that way. Beck: Hmm. Odell: And so I just simply stopped going. It was a totally unremarkable thing. I didn’t even tell anyone, Oh, I’m quitting Facebook. I just stopped going to it. And I think that’s really powerful. So that’s why I’m a big fan of anything that can give someone sort of granular control over what the—it sort of reintroduced choice in areas where people have never experienced choice. Because that, in and of itself, will cause someone to reflect upon what it is that they want. Beck: All of this reminds me of a study I’ve been thinking of a lot lately, that found using an app that was similar to the Brick for two weeks had such a big effect on people’s attention spans that it amounted to, like, reversing 10 years of cognitive decline— Beck: Oh my God. Beck: —which seems really huge. Odell: Wow. That’s incredible. I’m surprised and not surprised. Actually, honestly, this reminds me of, like, ecological restoration because when you restore a site, some things come back quickly and some things don’t, right? Like, you restore a wetland, some species are gonna come back almost immediately. The nutrient cycling of the entire site might take 100 years. Maybe our attention is similar in that, or our behavior, let’s say, it takes a long time to totally overhaul something. But at the same time, I think you might be surprised at how quickly certain things change. Like, in times when I was a little bit more embroiled online and using my phone a lot, and then I would maybe go somewhere, put it away for a while or whatever, I found that after a couple of days, I would notice that my attention felt different. Beck: Hmm. Odell: And by attention felt different, I mean I would notice details or small differences in things. It’s almost like having a higher-resolution image or something. Beck: Are there other seemingly small changes to your routine that you feel like might have that kind of big cognitive benefit? Odell: You know, I think trying to replace habits with other habits—I meditate in the morning, only just for, like, 10 minutes. I kind of calm down to a level where then it’s not going to as easily occur to me to then pick up my phone, or at least I'll be a little bit more reflective about it. Beck: Yeah. My thing so far, my recent thing has been taking up knitting and crochet, and this seems so small, but it’s like now while I’m watching TV, instead of looking at my phone, my hands are in hand jail, right? Doing knitting. Odell: ( Laughs. ) Hand jail. Beck: And it doesn’t seem so virtuous when I’m like, Now I’m only looking at one screen , but I feel like, you know, it’s an improvement. Odell: I think that’s great. Beck: Maybe I'll get down to zero screens, TBD. But the other layer to that that I was just thinking about when it comes to phones and social media and stuff is, like, a lot of times where I’m going to learn how to do this new stitch or whatever is YouTube. Odell: Mm-hmm. Beck: So it’s not, you know, one is totally replacing the other, but there is sort of a relationship. Like now I am using that tool kind of for this other thing. Odell: Yeah. Right, and I think that points to an important distinction, which is maybe a bit more nuanced than just, say, screen time as a statistic. You know, you were asking earlier about my changed relationship to my phone. Beck: Mm-hmm. Odell: I think about it more as like: When I look at it as an object, it looks like a tool. And it did not look like a tool to me before. It looked like a black hole. Beck: Like a portal to the underworld or something. Odell: Yeah. Or, frankly, I wasn’t even looking at it. I’m already picking it up. Like, I’m already in there. I’m already in that world. There wasn’t even a point where I perceived the phone as an object. Beck: Yeah. You skipped right ahead. Odell: Yeah. And now I feel like the things that I use it for: the Merlin app, it’s like Shazam for bird songs, I use that. I use iNaturalist. I use the Constellation app, voice memos for, you know, recording birds. That relationship, to me, feels really different because the intention and the purpose, I feel like I’m in control of that. I mean on my phone, the first home screen is all what I would call observational apps, so camera, voice memo, iNaturalist, Merlin. Beck: Mm. Odell: I’m kind of trying to remind myself of how I wanna use the phone. Like, I now associate my phone with those activities. Beck: You write a lot about nature. Odell: Yeah. Beck: Being inspired by nature, how being in nature helps you, you know, pay attention. A common piece of advice for those who have been brain-rotted by the internet is to go touch grass. So are you also telling us to touch grass? Odell: Yeah, pretty much. And, I mean, the weeds that I weed at my weekly project are grass, so— Beck: And you’re touching them. Odell: —actually, I’m saying Kill grass . No, I’m just kidding. ( Laughs. ) But the reason I think it became such a—that phrase caught on was because it’s just so obviously true. The obvious truth of it is, like, why it’s funny and annoying at the same time. Beck: Yeah. What is it that you think the natural world has to teach us about attention? Odell: Complexity, basically. Like, I think it's a master class in complexity. It is kind of an antidote to the idea of the easy answer, which I think—I really blame Instagram for the oversimplification of political issues.Like, personally, that is just my ax to grind. And the idea that you could sort of absolve yourself by reposting something is just—yeah. It’s upsetting to me. But I think that there’s no easy answers to anything. Like, if you are a birder and you like birds, well, guess what? You’re gonna have to learn about trees. Beck: Mm-hmm. Odell: And then gonna have to learn about, like, seasons, and then, I don’t know, there’s just—everything is so tied to everything else, and there are so many things that are sort of, like, neither good nor bad or sort of arguable. We need lessons in that right now. Like, we need lessons in the sort of, like, Let me pick a point in space to look at, and then let me look at the context around that. Okay, now let me look at the context around that. And now you’ve sort of widened this whole ecosystem. I think the opposite of that is what happens online. Beck: So Jenny, if someone is just starting to rethink the relationship they have with their devices, what advice would you give them? Odell: Try to take an outsider’s perspective on yourself. I’m a big journaler, so I’ve journaled since I was a kid. So that would work for me. I would look at my phone, I would look at some stuff on my phone, and then I would just write down, kinda what it was and then how I felt about it. And I would be, like, brutally honest. Beck: Oh, man. Odell: Just pretend like you’re a scientist. And just talk to a friend about it. You could write it down, like, whatever. But, you know, I think there needs to be that, like, every so often you step to the side and you go, Okay, what did I just do? Like, Why did I do that? How did that make me feel? You can be super brief about it. Just do it for a week. Just see what it tells you. Beck: Yeah. Odell: Before you try to make any changes, because the danger is that a person feels shame, they feel that it’s bad. They’re like, Okay, I need to change this , and then they try really hard to change it, and then it doesn’t go the way they wanted, and then they feel more shame. And now it’s just, like, a spiral. Beck: Yeah. I think especially with attention for whatever reason, it does feel very shameful, this like, Oh, I can’t focus; I can’t pay attention. I can’t even, like, read a book without having the desire to pick up my phone. Odell: Yeah. And people think it means that they’re a bad person, and it doesn’t. You just gotta be patient and try a bunch of different things and maybe it’ll be more interesting than you think. [ Music ] Beck: Guys, huge news. Huge news. I locked my gym locker today. Nature is healing. I am the virus. For once in my goddamn life, I locked my gym locker. It is day 13. I was on the computer all day for work because computer is where the money comes from. You can still screen fatigue yourself. ( Laughs. ) The old-fashioned way. Captain’s log, the final full day of the experiment. Over the past two weeks, I read one full novel, I started two other books, I finished an audiobook, I crocheted a hat, I watched all of the first season of The Traitors . It’s not like I, you know, found myself with a magical abundance of time. I think it’s more like I just paid more attention and spent more time doing the things that I already like to do. That was time mostly well spent, so attention mostly well spent. Brennan: Julie, when you set out to go on this experiment you got in touch with one of the researchers from the 2025 study, Kostadin Kushlev from Georgetown University, who agreed to go over the results of your post-experiment attention test with us. And before we call him up, are you nervous about your results, not so nervous about these results? Will it mean less to you if your attention span didn’t change on paper? Beck: I mean, I guess I’m a little nervous. I mean, look, I am a nerd and I always wanna get an A+ on my projects. But I really do feel better, and if it’s just a placebo effect, well, a placebo effect is still an effect, right? Like, I’ll take it. Brennan: Okay, I’m gonna dial Kosta up. [ Phone ringing ] Kostadin Kushlev: Hello. Brennan: Hi, I’m Natalie. I'm Julie’s producer. I’m also gonna be sitting in on this call. Kushlev: Hi, Natalie. Beck: Hey, Kosta. It’s Julie. How are you? Kushlev: Pretty good. How are you doing? Beck: I’m doing OK! So, can we just dive right in? Kushlev: Yes. Beck: And tell me, before I started the experiment, how was my baseline attention span? Kushlev: So your score was about three, 3.02. Beck: Is that good? Good for a 35-year-old? Good, bad? Kushlev: That’s pretty good. Essentially, you did about how our participants did. It’s a little closer to the level you might see in young adulthood or for somebody in their 60s. ( Laughs. ) Beck: ( Laughs. ) Okay. Humbling. Humbling. Kushlev: Yes. Yes. But, you know, but once we get to your post score— Beck: Yes, let’s do it. Kushlev: — things really change. Beck: The big reveal. Kushlev: Yes. Beck: What changed? Kushlev: So your post score was actually hugely better. So it was 3.8. And that is much bigger improvement than we saw on average in our study. So your improvement is about four to five times bigger than what the average participant in our study gained. Brennan: Go Julie! Beck: Write it down, Natalie. Write it down. ( Laughs. ) Brennan: I’m taking notes. Kushlev: Yeah. So you did really well on that. Beck: Amazing, I think. Is 3.1 to 3.8 good? Have I reversed my cognitive decline? Or how would you characterize that? Kushlev: You’re basically off the charts. Beck: ( Laughs. ) Kushlev : But it might take a while to reap the benefits of this improved attention. Beck: Right. And it’ll probably go away if I just start scrolling Instagram again. Kushlev: Right. Yeah. Brennan: ( Laughs. ) Kushlev: It’s certainly not a permanent increase. But I do like to point out that, you know, just taking a two-week break and not even a complete break from your phone, just sort of like reducing your use, can actually improve that ability to sustain attention. Our lives are just like so tied to these devices, so sometimes the question might be: Have we like essentially permanently damaged our, you know— Beck: Yeah. Kushlev: —brains? Like, have we changed our neurobiology and so forth? And so this seems to suggest that no, there is a way out. So it might be worth doing some of those digital-detox interventions. [ Music ] Beck: Thank you so much, Kosta. It was great chatting with you! Kushlev: Alright, thank you, bye. Brennan: Bye! Brennan: Julie? Beck: Mm-hmm. Brennan: How do you feel about that? Beck: Unbearably smug. No, no, no. I’m just kidding. No, I feel relieved, honestly. Like, even if the true effect size isn’t as big as it seemed, ’cause I am just one person; it’s not, you know, a full scientific study— Brennan: Yeah. Beck: —it still feels really good to know that it’s possible to improve so quickly. Brennan: Right. Beck: So it’s actually kind of wild that you can do something as simple as this and, like, bounce back so quickly. Brennan: Are you going to keep using the Brick? Like, how are you feeling about—where’s your relationship at between you and your phone right now? Beck: My relationship with my phone is cordial. We’re not—it’s not warm— Brennan: ( Laughs. ) Beck : —but it’s not cold. We’re cordial. We’re friendly acquaintances. Brennan: That sounds like how people describe their exes. Beck: Yeah. And, well, we haven’t broken up. It really is—it’s a situationship— Brennan: Totally. Beck: —that is ongoing forever. No, I’m definitely gonna continue using the Brick, and I have been still. Twenty-three hours a day? You know, maybe not. Brennan: Yeah. Beck: I have been Bricking my phone, at a minimum, before bed, so I can't doom scroll right before I sleep, and I can’t look at my emails or Instagram the second that I regain consciousness. So that does help. [ Music ] But I would say that throughout this, I kept thinking about my favorite poet, Mary Oliver, and one thing that she wrote was, “To pay attention, this is our endless and proper work.” Brennan: That’s beautiful. Beck: So this season, I think what I’ve learned is: Your attention is your life. And I think on some level I knew that already, but after this experiment, I’ve really been feeling it. Brennan: We started this season because we wanted to understand why so many people were feeling the pull to log off, right? We’ve explored a lot of the ways in which the internet can pull you into thoughtless patterns, whether it’s the way Instagram makes us feel bad about our bodies or the way that AI chatbots can send us into an anxious spiral. But it seems like what we are maybe actually looking for, right now, is ways to be more thoughtful. Beck: Yeah, I wanted to feel more thoughtful about my life. I wanted to not to feel as much like I’m literally giving my life away to things that I don’t even care about. I wanted to stop nickel-and-diming the moments of my life away. Brennan: Being intentional about where you give your attention. [ Music ] Beck: That’s all for this season of How to Touch Grass . This episode was hosted by me, Julie Beck, and co-hosted and produced by Natalie Brennan, with production help from Elena Schwartz. Our editors are Claudine Ebeid and Jocelyn Frank. Fact-check by Gisela Salim-Peyer. Our engineers are Rob Smierciak and Miguel Carrascal. Rob also composed some of the music for this show. The executive producer of audio is Claudine Ebeid, and the managing editor of audio is Andrea Valdez. How To will be back with a new season soon.

items.title: Un poème pour la route | À quoi bon ?
items.description: Notre contributeur, économiste au long parcours, qui a sillonné le globe en long et en large, et dont les articles sur la situation de l’économie tunisienne font souvent le bonheur des lecteurs de Kapitalis, se découvre, à 70 ans passés, une âme de poète. Nous partageons ci-dessous son dernier poème. Sadok Zerelli À quoi bon courir après les heures, Quand le temps nous poursuit sans se lasser ? À quoi bon bâtir des demeures, Que le vent un jour viendra balayer ? À quoi bon les querelles et les rancunes, Les ambitions, les honneurs, les vanités, Quand nous sommes tous, poussière parmi les poussières, Des voyageurs égarés dans l’immensité ? Nous naissons sans avoir choisi de naître, Nous apprenons à marcher, à parler, à aimer, Puis nous passons notre vie à vouloir être Quelqu’un que le temps finira par oublier. Nous sommes de passage, Quelques battements dans l’immensité, Une poussière de lumière sur une page Que l’univers refermera un jour sans pitié Et pourtant… Il suffit d’un ciel bleu après la pluie, D’un camélia qui un matin fleurit, D’un poème écrit au milieu de la nuit, Pour qu’on aime la vie. L’article Un poème pour la route | À quoi bon ? est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: À Cuba, la crise énergétique fait fuir les touristes

items.title: Face aux Burkinabè vivant au Niger, le Président de l’Assemblée législative du Peuple appelle à l’unité et au patriotisme
items.description: En marge de son séjour à Niamey, le Président de l’Assemblée législative du Peuple, le Camarade Dr Ousmane BOUGOUMA, a rencontré ce dimanche 23 août la communauté Burkinabè vivant au Niger réunie à l’occasion de son assemblée générale. En présence de l’Ambassadeur du Burkina Faso au Niger, le Colonel-major Abdou DIALLO et du Président de l’Association des ressortissants Burkinabè au Niger, Ali Koka TINDANO, le Président de l’Assemblée législative du Peuple a tenu à saluer ses compatriotes et à leur souhaiter une bonne tenue de leur assemblée générale. Revenant sur sa présence à Niamey, le Camarade Dr Ousmane BOUGOUMA a expliqué que la délégation parlementaire Burkinabè est présente pour prendre part à l’installation et à la première session des Sessions confédérales des Parlements de l’AES. Une étape qui doit permettre de parachever la mise en place des institutions de la Confédération des États du Sahel. Le Chef du Parlement a rappelé que la Confédération repose sur trois principales instances à savoir le Collège des Chefs d’État, le Conseil des ministres et les Sessions confédérales des Parlements. Les deux premières étant déjà en place, les travaux de Niamey doivent permettre de mettre en place la troisième. Pour le Camarade Dr Ousmane BOUGOUMA, le Parlement confédéral doit avant tout porter la voix des peuples de l’AES. Il doit également contribuer à permettre aux populations de l’espace confédéral de vivre et d’exercer librement leurs activités dans les trois pays. S’adressant ensuite aux Burkinabè vivant au Niger, le Président de l’Assemblée législative du Peuple les a invités à rester dignes, intègres et patriotes, tout en respectant les lois du pays d’accueil. Il les a également encouragés à accompagner l’action de l’Ambassadeur du Burkina Faso au Niger et à préserver les liens qui unissent les compatriotes établis dans le pays. « Vous tous, sans exception, vous êtes des ambassadeurs du Burkina Faso au Niger », leur a-t-il rappelé avant d’insister sur la nécessité de l’union, de l’engagement et du patriotisme. Pour le Camarade Dr Ousmane BOUGOUMA, cette solidarité doit également s’inscrire dans une vision plus large, celle d’une communauté de peuples liés par un même espace confédéral. « Nous sommes une même famille », a-t-il déclaré, appelant ses compatriotes à se soutenir et à rester attachés à la mère patrie. Source : L'Assemblée législative du Peuple

Durant l'ete, son mouvement a multiplie les demonstrations de force avec ses universites d'ete mais aussi avec une veritable occupation du terrain mediatique. Une dynamique confortee par la mobilisation militante Un sondage Harris Interactive-Toluna pour M6 et RTL place Jean-Luc Melenchon entre 16 % et 17 % des intentions de vote, contre 12 % en avril. Dans plusieurs hypotheses, il se hisse au second tour face a Marine Le Pen (35 a 38 %), devancant ou egalant edouard Philippe. 🔴 Le sondage Toluna-Harris montre un premier tour ouvert à 8 mois de l’élection 🔴 JL Mélenchon 16 🟣 R Gluksmann 10 🟡 E Philippe 17 🔵 B Retailleau 7 ⚫️ M Le Pen 35 #Presidentielle2026 pic.twitter.com/xZbyY0MzMK — Les Progressistes (@_Progressistes) August 23, 2026 Cette progression survient au moment ou LFI a reuni plus de 8 000 participants aux Amfis de Châteauneuf-sur-Isere, l'universite d'ete de La France insoumise. « La France insoumise est prete a gouverner des 2027 », a martele Melenchon, qui a teinte son discours d'ecologie avec la « planification » et une « conscription ecologique ». Il n'y a d'autre solution que la victoire électorale et le changement radical de politique. Dans une élection présidentielle, ce qui compte, ce n'est pas le nombre de candidatures, c'est le nombre d'électeurs. Rien ne doit empêcher l'unité populaire. La rupture programmatique… pic.twitter.com/CGlNhCb4PQ — Jean-Luc Mélenchon (@JLMelenchon) August 23, 2026 Le mouvement se targue d'etre « plus puissant sur tous les points » qu'en 2022, en militants, parlementaires et programme. a gauche, la concurrence apparaît limitee. Raphael Glucksmann, qui vient d'officialiser sa candidature, plafonne autour de 10 %. LFI tend la main aux ecologistes a condition qu'ils soutiennent Melenchon, tandis que les polemiques contre les prefets ou le budget a venir du gouvernement maintiennent le mouvement a la une. Sur X, le depute Hadrien Clouet a ironise sur la candidature Glucksmann : « M. Glucksmann a parle. Jean-Luc Melenchon a gagne 1 point ». Il n'y a d'autre solution que la victoire électorale et le changement radical de politique. Dans une élection présidentielle, ce qui compte, ce n'est pas le nombre de candidatures, c'est le nombre d'électeurs. Rien ne doit empêcher l'unité populaire. La rupture programmatique… pic.twitter.com/CGlNhCb4PQ — Jean-Luc Mélenchon (@JLMelenchon) August 23, 2026 La dynamique a gauche semble en effet tres favorable au candidat insoumis, qui progresse dans les sondages en depit des attaques politiques et mediatiques. Le possible rassemblement des ecologistes, divise sur la question du candidat , pourrait parfaire la strategie de Jean-Luc Melenchon et donner un signal d'ouverture dans sa campagne electorale.

items.title: LASU assures qualified English students won’t spend extra year
items.description: The management of Lagos State University (LASU), Ojo, has assured students that no qualified student will spend an extra year at the institution due to missing results. The assurance followed reports that about 100 final-year students in the Department of English were at risk of spending an additional year after some of their 300-level results were allegedly not uploaded by two lecturers. The development sparked reactions on social media, particularly on X, amid concerns that the affected students could be unable to graduate with their colleagues. However, LASU, in a statement issued on Sunday, said the issue had been resolved after an investigation by the university management. “Following an enquiry by the University Management into the allegation concerning the non-upload of results of some graduating students in the Department of English, the University wishes to clarify that the Department has uploaded all outstanding results as of Sunday, 23 August 2026,” the statement reads. The university said students who had fulfilled all graduation requirements would graduate alongside their colleagues in the 2025/2026 academic session. “No student who has met all graduation requirements will be required to spend an extra year on account of the issue raised,” the institution said. It, however, clarified that students whose results remained outstanding after the latest action may not have completed all the requirements for graduation. “Any student whose result remains outstanding following this action has yet to fulfil the requirements for graduation and is advised to complete the necessary requirements accordingly.” LASU reiterated its commitment to ensuring that students who have fulfilled all graduation requirements are not unnecessarily delayed in completing their programmes. The post LASU assures qualified English students won’t spend extra year appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nvidia: des serveurs d’IA annoncés en hausse de plus de 15 %
items.description: Plusieurs grands clients de Nvidia ont été prévenus que le prix de serveurs équipés de ses puces d’IA pourrait augmenter de plus de 15 % dans de nombreux cas. La hausse, attribuée au coût de la mémoire, viserait des systèmes livrés au début de 2027. Le budget des grands centres de données pourrait encore s’alourdir. Selon une information de Bloomberg reprise le 22 août par Reuters et Channel NewsAsia, certains des plus importants clients de Nvidia ont été informés que le prix de serveurs intégrant ses accélérateurs d’intelligence artificielle augmenterait de plus de 15 % dans de nombreux cas. Les nouvelles grilles concerneraient des machines expédiées au début de 2027. Les systèmes cités comprennent les plateformes Vera Rubin et Grace Blackwell, deux générations au cœur des projets de calcul intensif. L’ampleur exacte de la hausse varierait selon la génération de puces et la configuration mémoire. Bloomberg relie le mouvement à l’envolée du coût des mémoires utilisées dans ces serveurs. Les fabricants sous contrat qui assemblent les machines pour des opérateurs tels que Microsoft, Google et Oracle auraient commencé à prévenir leurs propres clients. Cette information demeure attribuée à des personnes proches du processus. Reuters précise ne pas avoir pu la vérifier immédiatement et Nvidia n’avait pas répondu à sa demande de commentaire en dehors des heures ouvrables. Aucun tarif public détaillé, aucun calendrier par constructeur et aucune liste exhaustive de contrats concernés n’ont été publiés. Le pourcentage ne doit donc pas être appliqué automatiquement à chaque serveur ou à chaque commande. Pour les entreprises qui planifient un projet d’IA, une hausse sur le serveur complet touche davantage que la puce. La mémoire, les cartes réseau, le stockage, l’alimentation et le refroidissement entrent dans le coût final. Un devis signé, un prix catalogue et un coût livré peuvent aussi évoluer différemment selon les volumes, les délais et les clauses négociées. Les projets dont le financement est arrêté plusieurs mois avant la livraison sont les plus exposés à un écart budgétaire. Nvidia doit publier ses résultats du deuxième trimestre le 26 août. Cette échéance pourra apporter des indications sur la demande, les contraintes d’approvisionnement et les marges, sans garantir que l’entreprise détaille les prix négociés entre fabricants et opérateurs de centres de données. Les prochains devis commerciaux et les annonces des assembleurs permettront de mesurer si le niveau supérieur à 15 % devient fréquent ou reste limité à certaines configurations très riches en mémoire. La prudence reste donc nécessaire : l’augmentation rapportée est crédible par sa chaîne de sources, mais elle n’est pas encore confirmée directement par Nvidia. Pour les acheteurs, la conséquence immédiate consiste à réactualiser les devis plutôt qu’à multiplier une ancienne estimation par un taux unique. Les options de mémoire et les dates d’expédition devront apparaître clairement dans chaque offre révisée. Cet article vous est proposé en collaboration avec Aïobi . Contact : team@aiobi.world L’article Nvidia: des serveurs d’IA annoncés en hausse de plus de 15 % est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: 'Imran would not have spent 3 years in jail if he wanted to make a deal,' says PTI's Gohar
items.description: ISLAMABAD: PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Monday brushed aside speculation regarding a deal with the government, saying party founder Imran Khan would not have spent three years in jail if he wanted to make a deal. He made the remarks while speaking outside the Supreme Court (SC) alongside PTI leader Sardar Latif Khosa after the two met with the court’s registrar. “Khan sahib does not make deals. He will not stay in the hospital a minute more than is necessary for his tests and treatment. If he had to make a deal, he would not have spent three years in jail,” Gohar said. “All we have to say is that there should be no politics on his health,” he said. During the press talk, Gohar said that he and Khosa had arrived at the SC to meet with Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi in connection with the party’s contempt petition against the government’s alleged violation of its Aug 18 order for shifting Imran to Shifa International Hospital. “I asked to meet the chief justice. He was busy so it could not happen. Myself and Khosa sahib met the SC registrar and requested that a number be allotted to this case and it be fixed for hearing,” he said. He said that the registrar had assured that a case number would be allotted to the contempt plea. Gohar said that they were also assured of the early fixation of the case before the SC. “This [Aug 18 order] cannot be ignored. The whole world is looking at the SC and whether it is able to implement its order,” he said. “We only wanted PTI founder’s medical tests to be conducted at a private hospital, with both his sister Uzma and his personal physician Dr Faisal Sultan included in the medical board examining him,” he said. Meanwhile, Khosa said that a case number was being allotted to the was in Lahore. Last week, Imran’s sister Uzma Khan had filed contempt petition before the SC against officials for flouting its Aug 18 order. The petition, filed by Advocate Uzair Karamat Bhandari on behalf of Dr Uzma, also requested the apex court to depute an officer or appoint a local commission to ensure that Imran was immediately shifted to the private hospital in accordance with its earlier directions. Imran’s hospital transfer saga Last week, the SC had ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board. A three-member bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed and comprising Justices Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Ishtiaq Ibr­ahim issued the interim contempt petition, and quoted the registrar as saying that one of the judges directions on petitions seeking Imran’s hospitalisation, access to personal physicians and family members and provision of his medical record to his family. The court had also ordered that Dr Uzma and Dr Sultan — Imran’s personal physician — be present during the medical check-up by a medical board. At the same time, Imran’s family members, PTI members and lawyers associated with him were barred from disclosing his health condition or medical reports to the media or public until the next hearing. The next day, the government had filed a review plea against the court’s order to shift Imran to the private hospital, arguing that the directive was discriminatory and issued in violation of prison rules and principles of natural justice. However, the SC had returned the plea on Thursday with the objection that the contents of the affidavit and facts, along with the review petition filed under Article 188 of the Constitution, had not been properly drawn up and that one of the paper books was not in order. The same night, elaborate arrangements were put in place in and around Shifa International Hospital, and all signs pointed to the PTI founder being brought there, in compliance with the SC order. But, it became clear on Friday morning that Imran had been taken to Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) for a check-up and then subsequently transported back to prison. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar blamed “the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside Al Shifa Hospital” for the diversion. In a post on X, he said, “In the light of the SC’s order, the prisoner was taken to the hospital under appropriate security arrangements during the night between August 20 and 21. “A team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist, and a physician, conducted a detailed examination of him and declared him medically fit,” he said. Later, the Pims administration said that two specialists from Shifa Inter­national Hospital participated in Imran’s eye assessment, while other examinations were carried out by the concerned Pims specialists. Imran has been taken to Pims multiple times after his eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January. “The clinical input arising from the ophthalmological assessment was taken into account alongside findings of the investigations conducted at Pims,” the statement said. Meanwhile, the government on Thursday filed a fresh review petition against the SC’s Aug 18 order. The Islamabad chief commissioner again filed the plea, saying that his office had a direct, substantial and legally protected interest in the matter and that the Aug 18 order adversely affected its constitutional authority.

items.title: Cameroun: l’AVC, première cause de mortalité chez les femmes
items.description: © DR Les maladies cérébrovasculaires tuent le plus les femmes au Cameroun avec 9,0% des décès, suivies des affections périnatales à 7,0% et du diabète à 4,7%, selon les dernières données du ministère de la Santé. C’est une réalité alarmante pour la santé féminine. Au Cameroun, l’accident vasculaire cérébral, AVC, est désormais la première cause initiale de décès chez les femmes. Selon les chiffres publiés dans un graphique «Top 10 des causes initiales chez les femmes», issus de la source « MINSANTE, DHIS2/ICD-11 – Cause of Death-2025 / ANACoD3 », la « Maladie cérébrovasculaire » représente à elle seule «9.0% » des cas. En deuxième position, les «Affections survenant au cours de la période périnatale» avec «7.0% », un indicateur qui pèse lourd sur la mortalité néonatale liée à la mère. Le trio de tête est complété par les maladies métaboliques : «Diabète sucré» à «4.7%» et «Troubles endocriniens » à «4.3%». Les maladies infectieuses restent pourtant meurtrières. Le «Paludisme» cause «4.1%» des décès féminins et le «VIH» « 3.8%». Le classement se poursuit avec la «Néphrite et néphrose » à «3.3%», les «Infections des voies respiratoires inférieures » à «3.2%», la «Maladie hypertensive» à «3.1%» et enfin les «Affections maternelles» à « 2.8%». Des données qui interpellent sur l’urgence de la prévention des maladies non transmissibles chez les femmes. Cet article Cameroun: l'AVC, première cause de mortalité chez les femmes est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Décès de Abderrahmane Tlili | Le parcours heurté d’un homme controversé
items.description: Décédé le dimanche 23 août 2026, à l’âge de 83 ans, Abderrahmane Tlili était un commis de l’Etat, un activiste politique et un homme d’affaires assez controversé dont le parcours, en dents de scie, n’a pas été un long fleuve tranquille. Latif Belhedi Fils de Ahmed Tlili, l’ancien secrétaire général de l’Union générale tunisienne du travail (UGTT), qui s’était illustré par son opposition à la dérive dictatoriale de Habib Bourguiba, Abderrahmane Tlili n’a pas eu de scrupules à louer ses services au même Bourguiba ainsi qu’à son successeur, non moins dictateur, Zine El Abidine Ben Ali, avec lequel il s’était, cependant, brouillé à la fin, non pour des raisons politiques, mais pour des affaires d’argent. Ce qui lui valut des démêlées judiciaires et des incarcérations pour de présumés abus commis dans la gestion de l’Office de l’aviation civile et des aéroports (Oaca) qu’il avait dirigé jusqu’à sa remise à la retraite d’office en 2003. Commis de l'ETat, le défunt a été Pdg de l’Office national de l’huile pendant 11 ans, de la Société de transport pétrolier saharien pendant 5 ans, de la Compagnie franco-tunisienne de pétrole pendant 2 ans, de la Société italo-tunisienne de pétrole pendant 4 ans et de l’Oaca pendant 3 ans. En politique, il a démarré sa carrière au sein du Parti socialiste destourien (PSD), au pouvoir, et de son héritier le Rassemblement constitutionnel démocratique (RCD), fondé en 1988 par Zine El-Abidine Ben Ali, avant de fonder, en 1988, à la demande de ce dernier, l'Union démocratique unioniste (UDU) d'obédience nationaliste arabe, l’un des partis du décor démocratique qui servaient d’alibi pour le dictateur de l’époque pour réprimer les vrais partis de l’opposition et les empêcher de participer aux comédies électorales. Pour avoir servi avec zèle Ben Ali, dont il était très proche, que ses déboires avec une justice à la solde de ce dernier ne lui ont pas valu beaucoup de soutien de la part de la société civile, qui voyait dans ces déboires des règlements de comptes au sein d’un système corrompu jusqu’à la moelle. En juillet 2004, Abderrahmane Tlili est reconnu coupable de «délits d'abus de pouvoir, de violation des procédures légales en matière de conclusion de marchés publics et de change» . Et il est condamné à 9 ans de prison ferme et à une amende de 42,7 millions de dinars; il est également condamné à une amende supplémentaire de 6,7 millions de dinars à titre de réparation du préjudice matériel subi par l'Oaca et à 100 000 dinars pour le préjudice moral occasionné. Ses défenseurs avaient cependant souligné que «ni l’instruction judiciaire, ni le tribunal, n’ont pu établir la moindre preuve matérielle tangible justifiant ces peines». Il sera libéré le 17 janvier 2011, trois jours après la chute de Ben Ali. Le défunt avait vécu un grand drame personnel : son épouse, le docteur Saloua Tlili, a trouvé la mort le 3 juin 2003 à la suite d'une chute du premier étage du hall de l’aéroport international de Tunis-Carthage où se trouvaient alors les bureaux de son époux. Selon des amis du couple, elle souffrait d’une dépression nerveuse et se serait suicidée. Cet épisode fit beaucoup jaser à Tunis, parmi les adversaires du défunt comme parmi ses amis. L’article Décès de Abderrahmane Tlili | Le parcours heurté d’un homme controversé est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Cameroun : désactivation des téléphones non dédouanés dès le 1er septembre 2026
items.description: © DR Le ministre des Finances, Louis Paul Motaze, clarifie dans une note, la date du début effectif de la désactivation des terminaux de la contrebande sur le réseau national ainsi que des mesures de vérification du statut des appareils connectés et d'acquittement des frais exigibles. C'est la dernière ligne droite avant la mise hors réseau des téléphones activés en violation des exigences douanières. Le ministre des Finances, Louis Paul Motaze, invite les propriétaires détenant ces téléphones et ayant reçu des messages de notification ainsi que ceux n'ayant pas reçu de notification à s'arrimer à la règle. À défaut, leurs téléphones seront désactivés à compter du 1er septembre 2026. Ils en ont encore pour sept jours. Sont concernés par la désactivation qui s'annonce, les téléphones non dédouanés qui se connecteront sur le réseau local de télécommunications pour la première fois ; les téléphones non dédouanés qui s'étant connectés après le 1er avril 2026 ont reçu des messages d'information mais restés dans suite ; les téléphones non dédouanés qui, activés de manière groupée par la même SIM, après le 1er avril 2026 n'ont pas fait l'objet d'utilisation continue. Les détenteurs de ces appareils peuvent s'assurer de leur statut (conforme ou non conforme) en vérifiant à travers les canaux indiqués. Il s'agit de relever l'IMEI du téléphone en composant *#06# ; de vérifier le statut via la plateforme www.mpie.camcis.cm ou en contactant la direction générale des douanes au 8044. Les personnes ou structures peuvent s'acquitter des droits de douane via le canal http://ept.camcis.cm/ept/longin?reason=dclrTrmn . Le ministre des Finances rappelle que la réforme des exigeant la nouvelle procédure de paiement de taxe de douane des téléphones importés est contenue dans l'article 6 de la loi de finances pour l'exercice 2023. L'application de cette disposition étant à la phase finale, il sera question de refuser l'accès aux réseaux locaux de télécommunications à ceux des appareils activés en contournant le paiement des taxes. Dans une communication en date du 26 avril 2027, près d'un mois après la date fixée pour le début effectif de ces paiements, le ministère des Finances a signalé que 700 000 nouveaux téléphones ont été connectés pour la première fois au réseau local entre le 1er et le 25 avril 2026 sans toutefois payer les taxes de douane. Le ministère, optant pour la sensibilisation avant la répression, a alors donné du temps pour que les propriétaires ou vendeurs se conforment à la règle. Quelque temps après, le directeur général des douanes a donné l'instruction aux directeurs de MTN et de Orange de procéder au blocage des téléphones non dédouanés à partir du 25 mai 2026. Avec la nouvelle date de blocage fixée au 1er septembre, il est à se demander si au final l'opération connaîtra son aboutissement. Cet article Cameroun : désactivation des téléphones non dédouanés dès le 1er septembre 2026 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Houet : AS Dafra remporte la 8e édition du tournoi Bien-être Enfant
items.description: Houet : AS Dafra remporte la 8e édition du tournoi Bien-être Enfant Bobo-Dioulasso, 24 août 2026 (AIB) – L’Association sportive de Dafra (AS Dafra) de Sarfalao a remporté, le dimanche 23 août 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso, la 8e édition du tournoi Bien-être Enfant, en s’imposant en finale face à SAM Académie de Lafiabougou sur le score de 2 buts à 0, au terme de deux fois 30 minutes de jeu. Placée sous le thème « Promouvoir la paix et le développement par l’éducation sportive des enfants », la compétition a réuni 24 équipes de la catégorie U15 de la ville de Bobo-Dioulasso. En finale, l’AS Dafra, vêtue de jaune, a dominé SAM Académie de Lafiabougou grâce à deux réalisations, décrochant ainsi son troisième sacre consécutif dans cette compétition. L’équipe victorieuse est repartie avec un trophée, un jeu de maillots, des ballons, des médailles en or et une enveloppe financière. La formation classée deuxième a reçu un jeu de maillots, des ballons, des médailles en argent et une enveloppe financière. La présidente de la délégation spéciale de l’arrondissement 6 de Bobo-Dioulasso, Salamata Compaoré/Sinaré, a salué la tenue de la compétition jusqu’à sa huitième édition. « Ce n’est pas donné à n’importe qui d’initier une activité et de la tenir jusqu’à la huitième édition. Nous avons également vu les différents prix et je peux dire que le jeu de la finale entre les deux équipes était à la hauteur. Cela prouve que, du début jusqu’à aujourd’hui, elles ne sont pas arrivées en finale par hasard. Elles ont mérité leur place », a-t-elle déclaré. Camarade Compaoré/Sinaré a assuré de son accompagnement aux initiatives visant à occuper sainement la jeunesse. « Toutes les questions qui vont réunir la jeunesse et qui peuvent occuper sainement la jeunesse, nous serons toujours présents, si la santé et notre temps nous le permettent », a-t-elle ajouté, soulignant la nécessité de préparer le football burkinabè dès le bas âge. Pour le promoteur du tournoi, Dominique Kouda, cette édition, à l’instar des précédentes, vise à occuper sainement les enfants pendant les vacances. « C’est une façon pour nous de les retrouver, de les réunir à un endroit, et cela permet d’éviter certains vices de la société. C’est l’occasion également de permettre à ceux qui ont des talents de se faire valoir et de pouvoir se tracer une carrière footballistique », a-t-il expliqué. Camarade Kouda s’est dit satisfait de la qualité du jeu, de la mobilisation et du fair-play observé tout au long de la compétition. Il a invité les équipes participantes à davantage de sérieux et d’application, estimant que « cela paye toujours ». Agence d'Information du Burkina CS/AB/wis

items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a entamé ses échanges en hausse lundi, son indice phare, le MASI, progressant de 0,71% à 19.127,90 points (pts). Pour sa part, le MASI Mid and Small Cap, qui reflète la performance des petites et moyennes capitalisations, avançait de 0,38% à 1.813,85 pts. À l'opposé, Involys (-3,71% à 127,10 DH), SNP (-2,68% à 360,10 DH), Label Vie (-2,38% à 4.100 DH), Risma (-1,76% à 321,25 DH) et Stroc Industrie (-1,60% à 182 DH) accusaient les plus fortes baisses. items.title: Sanaba : le CSPS de Ziga lance le deuxième passage de la campagne CPS Plus
items.description: Burkina-Bankui-Santé-Campagne-vaccination Sanaba : le CSPS de Ziga lance le deuxième passage de la campagne CPS Plus Ziga, 24 août 2026 (AIB) – Le Centre de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS) de Ziga, dans la commune de Sanaba, province des Banwa, a entamé le jeudi 20 août 2026, le deuxième passage de la campagne nationale de Chimio-prévention du paludisme saisonnier (CPS Plus), sous la conduite de l’infirmier chef de poste (ICP), le major Faissale Sanogo. La campagne s’est déroulée du 20 au 23 août 2026, et a ciblé les enfants âgés de 3 à 59 mois. Elle a été menée par le personnel de santé, avec l’appui des agents de santé à base communautaire (ASBC) et des distributeurs communautaires. Dès le premier jour, plusieurs équipes ont été déployées dans les différents quartiers de Ziga afin d’assurer une large couverture. Elles ont privilégié la stratégie du porte-à-porte, sillonnant les concessions pour administrer le traitement préventif aux enfants éligibles. Selon l’ICP Faissale Sanogo, ce deuxième passage comporte quatre principales interventions. Il s’agit du dépistage de la malnutrition aiguë chez les enfants de 6 à 59 mois, de l’administration du traitement de la CPS aux enfants de 3 à 59 mois, de l’identification des enfants de 5 à 23 mois dont le calendrier de vaccination contre le paludisme n’est pas à jour et de la destruction des gîtes larvaires. Pour Moidi Konaté, un habitant de Ziga, cette campagne constitue une opportunité de renforcer la prévention du paludisme chez les enfants de moins de cinq ans, particulièrement vulnérables pendant la saison des pluies. Il a invité les mères et les personnes ayant la charge des enfants à rester dans leurs concessions afin de faciliter le passage des équipes. L’ICP a, pour sa part, exhorté les ASBC et les distributeurs communautaires à poursuivre la sensibilisation des populations sur les autres moyens de prévention du paludisme, notamment l’utilisation des moustiquaires imprégnées et l’assainissement du cadre de vie. « Protéger les enfants contre le paludisme, c’est protéger notre avenir », a-t-il affirmé. Agence d’information du Burkina LRS/SO/wis
